facts: In the section The Last Days of Death, Harari says the UN right to life turns death into a rights violation.
Religions sanctified life beyond this world and so tolerated death. Harari asks the reader to picture Christianity, Islam or Hinduism in a world without death.
For modern people, he writes, death is a technical problem we can and should solve. Engineers replace priests as experts on death; a few geeks in a lab can do it.
He calls the effort the Gilgamesh Project.

He cites Google's Calico, whose stated aim is to solve death, as an early step. Calico was announced on 18 September 2013 and led by Arthur Levinson; Google itself spoke of the challenge of aging and associated diseases.
Modern medicine has not lengthened natural life by a year; it has prevented premature death.
Equality is out, immortality is in; he expects the fight for eternal youth to become the fiercest political battle.
A reviewer says treating death as only a technical problem presents a contested view as settled.
Gilgamesh Project aims: nanobot immune systems clearing arteries, fighting bacteria and cancer, slowing or stopping aging; death as a technical failure.
In a 2016 talk Harari guessed overcoming death would take centuries, not decades.
scene_details: A company named Calico with the stated aim of solving death
A few geeks in a lab in place of priests
tension: A company says it aims to solve death while the book says medicine has not added a year to natural life.
opening_idea: Start with the stated aim of Calico, then back up to what the book says about priests and engineers.

lessons.idea: How you name a problem decides who you hand it to.
lessons.anchor: Harari says modern people call death a technical problem and so hand it to engineers instead of priests.
lessons.everyday_example_idea: A family that calls grandpa's forgetfulness a scheduling problem and buys a calendar, rather than asking the doctor.

reflect_final: Which problem in your life have you named in a way that sends it to the wrong person for help?

use_cases.situation: A team calls a conflict a communication bug.
use_cases.move: Ask who we have handed it to by calling it that, as Harari says moderns did with death.

use_cases.situation: A dinner conversation turns to living forever.
use_cases.move: Ask whether you would want it if it cost more than most could pay, since Harari says equality is out and immortality is in.

use_cases.situation: You catch yourself treating a worry as a task list.
use_cases.move: Say what the problem is called in your head and who that name sends it to.

pocket_idea: Harari says we call death a technical problem and so hand it to engineers: the name you give a problem picks who tries to solve it.

conversation_variants.punchline_idea: Harari says modern people look at death the way engineers look at a broken machine.
conversation_variants.thirty_sec_idea: Harari says religions tolerated death and moderns treat it as a technical problem; Google launched Calico aiming to solve it; yet medicine has not added a year to natural lifespan.
